stories.headline: Canada launches $2.3B 'AI for All' strategy targeting 250,000 new jobs by 2031

key_facts.fact: Prime Minister Mark Carney launched Canada's national AI strategy on June 4, pledging more than CA$2.3 billion and targeting an additional CA$200 billion in economic growth.
key_facts.excerpt: Canada's federal government launched AI for All: Canada's new national artificial intelligence strategy on Thursday, pledging more than $2.3 billion and targeting an additional $200 billion in economic growth.

key_facts.fact: The strategy aims to create up to 90,000 AI-related jobs for young Canadians and 250,000 more jobs through AI adoption by 2031.
key_facts.excerpt: The strategy promises to create up to 90,000 AI-related jobs for young people. It also says up to 250,000 new jobs will be created through AI adoption by 2031.

key_facts.fact: Ottawa will put CA$500 million into a new Canadian Tech Growth Fund that will allow the federal government to take equity stakes in promising Canadian AI firms.
key_facts.excerpt: The government is also putting $500 million toward establishing a Canadian Tech Growth Fund. It says the fund 'will provide flexible growth capital and investment support, and enable the federal government, at times, to take equity stakes in the most promising Canadian AI firms.'

key_facts.fact: The plan targets raising Canadian business AI adoption from about 12% today to 60% by 2034 based on OECD modelling.
key_facts.excerpt: The government stated that business use of AI is targeted to rise from 12 per cent today to 60 per cent by 2034, based on Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) modelling.

key_facts.fact: Carney said Canada currently 'ranks near the bottom of countries in AI training, in literacy and trust,' framing the strategy as a 'pro-worker' adoption push.
key_facts.excerpt: Announcing the government's new AI strategy in Toronto on Thursday, Prime Minister Mark Carney said 'globally, Canada ranks near the bottom of countries in AI training, in literacy and trust.'

stories.headline: Cambridge team passes first human trial of an AI-designed 'super-antigen' vaccine

key_facts.fact: University of Cambridge researchers say this is the first time a vaccine's key component has been entirely designed by AI and trialled in humans.
key_facts.excerpt: The team at the University of Cambridge say it is the first time a vaccine's key component has been designed entirely by AI and then trialled in people.

key_facts.fact: The candidate, called pEVAC-PS, was tested in 39 healthy volunteers aged 18-50 and showed no significant safety concerns or serious adverse events, with results published in the Journal of Infection.
key_facts.excerpt: The open-label Phase 1 dose-escalation trial evaluated the vaccine candidate pEVAC-PS. The study involved 39 healthy volunteers between 18 and 50 years old... The results, published in the Journal of Infection, showed no significant safety concerns or serious adverse events.

key_facts.fact: The AI was fed genetic codes of coronaviruses and designed a 'super-antigen' aimed at protecting against an entire family of viruses, including bat-related coronaviruses that have not yet jumped to humans.
key_facts.excerpt: These genetic codes were analysed by an artificial intelligence. It then designed a 'super-antigen' that could train the immune system in such a way it gave protection against the whole family of viruses – even if they mutated or a new infection jumped from animals to people.

key_facts.fact: The vaccine was developed by Cambridge's Lab of Viral Zoonotics and spin-out DIOSynVax Ltd, sponsored by University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust with primary funding from Innovate UK.
key_facts.excerpt: The pEVAC-PS vaccine was developed by the University of Cambridge and its spin-out company, DIOSynVax Ltd... It was sponsored by the University Hospital Southampton NHS Foundation Trust, with primary funding from Innovate UK.

key_facts.fact: Researchers are now planning a Phase 2 trial in roughly 200 participants and are developing separate AI-designed candidates for flu and Ebola.
key_facts.excerpt: A second study – involving around 200 people – will give a greater understanding of how well it is training the immune system... the team is already developing separate vaccines that could tackle flu and Ebola.

key_facts.fact: Lead researcher Professor Jonathan Heeney said the work converts vaccine development 'from being reactive to being future-proof.'
key_facts.excerpt: 'We've converted vaccine development from being reactive to being future proof. Our vaccines will continue to provide protection against viruses even as they mutate into new strains,' said Jonathan, who leads the Lab of Viral Zoonotics.

stories.headline: China tightens oversight of its $3.4T private fund industry to steer money into tech

key_facts.fact: China's securities regulator on June 5 tightened oversight of the country's 23 trillion yuan ($3.40 trillion) private fund industry to reduce financial risks and channel capital into tech innovation.
key_facts.excerpt: China on Friday tightened oversight of the country's 23 trillion yuan ($3.40 trillion) private fund industry, in a bid to reduce financial risks and channel money into technology innovation and emerging industries.

key_facts.fact: The China Securities Regulatory Commission said it will raise the bar for private fund registration, crack down on illegal fund activities and encourage long-term 'patient' capital for tech-focused venture capital.
key_facts.excerpt: China's securities regulator said it would raise the bar for private fund registration, crack down on illegal fund activities and encourage long-term 'patient' capital to support tech-focused venture capital investments.

key_facts.fact: The move comes two weeks after Beijing launched a major crackdown on cross-border investment and tightened capital controls, and is part of a broader campaign to direct resources into the tech sector amid Sino-U.S. rivalry.
key_facts.excerpt: The announcement came two weeks after China launched a major crackdown on cross-border investment and tightened capital controls. It's also part of Beijing's broader campaign to direct resources into the tech sector, which is key in the Sino-U.S. power rivalry.

key_facts.fact: Regulators will set up a cross-agency monitoring platform to identify risks and misbehaviours and will step up monitoring of government-backed funds.
key_facts.excerpt: According to the latest rules, regulators will set up a cross-agency monitoring platform to identify risks and misbehaviours. The watchdog will also step up monitoring of operation by government-backed funds.

key_facts.fact: The new rules extend a clean-up that began in 2023 and has already deregistered more than 5,000 private fund managers.
key_facts.excerpt: The latest move represents a deepening of clean-up efforts that started in 2023 that saw the de-registration of more than 5,000 private fund managers.

stories.headline: Coinbase and Better fund first Fannie Mae-backed mortgage collateralized by bitcoin

key_facts.fact: Coinbase and Better Home & Finance Holding Company funded the first Fannie Mae-backed U.S. mortgage using bitcoin as collateral, with a nationwide rollout planned for summer 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Coinbase and Better have funded the first Fannie Mae-backed mortgage using bitcoin as collateral, with a nationwide rollout planned in the coming months.

key_facts.fact: The product pairs a standard 15- or 30-year Fannie Mae conforming mortgage with a separate privately-funded crypto-backed loan that covers the down payment, both at the same interest rate and consolidated into one monthly payment.
key_facts.excerpt: The structure involves two separate loans. Borrowers first receive a standard 15- or 30-year Fannie Mae-backed mortgage on the property itself. A second, privately financed loan — secured by pledged Bitcoin or USDC — covers the down payment. Both loans carry the same interest rate and term, consolidating into a single monthly payment.

key_facts.fact: Collateralization requires 250% for BTC and 125% for USDC, carries no margin calls, and the pledged crypto is held in Coinbase Prime custody and returned upon full repayment.
key_facts.excerpt: a private down-payment loan secured by BTC (250% collateral) or USDC (125% collateral), carries no margin calls, returns collateral on full repayment... The pledged crypto is held in Coinbase Prime custody for the life of the loan and returned upon full repayment.

key_facts.fact: Better's waitlist already represents about $250 million in potential loan volume, with more than half of interested borrowers planning to buy within six months.
key_facts.excerpt: The spokesperson said the waitlist currently represents around $250 million in potential loan volume, with more than half of interested borrowers looking to purchase a home within six months.

key_facts.fact: The regulatory pathway was cleared by a June 2025 Federal Housing Finance Agency directive instructing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to recognize digital assets as eligible collateral in the $18.5 trillion mortgage market.
key_facts.excerpt: The regulatory pathway was cleared in part by a June 2025 directive from the Federal Housing Finance Agency (FHFA) instructing Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac to recognize digital assets as eligible collateral in the $18.5 trillion mortgage market.

stories.headline: Israel-Lebanon ceasefire announced; oil dips on hopes of broader U.S.-Iran deal

key_facts.fact: The U.S. announced that Israel and Lebanon agreed to implement a ceasefire requiring Hezbollah to withdraw south of the Litani River and the Lebanese Armed Forces to take exclusive control of southern Lebanon.
key_facts.excerpt: The US said Lebanon and Israel have agreed to implement a ceasefire following talks in Washington, with the deal requiring an end to Hezbollah fire, the withdrawal of Hezbollah operatives from south of the Litani River, and the establishment of security zones under the exclusive control of Lebanese forces.

key_facts.fact: Brent crude fell about 1.6% to $96.25 a barrel and WTI fell 1.3% to $94.73 on June 4 as the ceasefire revived hopes of a broader U.S.-Iran agreement that could reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
key_facts.excerpt: Brent futures were down $1.56, or 1.6%, at $96.25 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude fell $1.29, or 1.3%, to $94.73.

key_facts.fact: The Republican-led U.S. House approved a resolution on June 3 to block President Trump from continuing the war against Iran; it would need Senate approval and two-thirds majorities in both chambers to override a likely veto.
key_facts.excerpt: In the U.S., the Republican-led House approved a resolution on Wednesday to block Trump from continuing the war against Iran. To take effect, the resolution would need Senate approval and two-thirds majorities in both chambers to override an almost certain Trump veto.

key_facts.fact: Trump said negotiations with Iran could see progress 'over the weekend,' while Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said contacts remain open but talks have made no progress.
key_facts.excerpt: US President Donald Trump said negotiations with Iran are going 'very well' and a deal to end the conflict 'could happen over the weekend'. However, he added, 'Who knows?'... Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said talks with the United States have made no progress, but channels of communication remain open.

key_facts.fact: Despite the ceasefire announcement, an Israeli drone strike wounded several people on the Zefta-Kfarwa Road in southern Lebanon, and analysts warn Strait of Hormuz shipping may take months to normalize.
key_facts.excerpt: A previous U.S.-brokered ceasefire announced in April failed to stop fighting, and exchanges of fire continued on Wednesday despite the latest diplomatic push.

stories.headline: Illinois Gov. Pritzker pauses data-center tax incentives from July 1 amid grid concerns

key_facts.fact: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker directed the state Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity to pause processing new agreements for data-center tax incentives starting July 1.
key_facts.excerpt: Governor JB Pritzker has directed the Illinois Department of Commerce and Economic Opportunity to pause processing new agreements for data center tax incentives. The pause for the Data Center Investment Program will start on July 1.

key_facts.fact: Pritzker called on lawmakers, labor groups, utilities, local governments and industry leaders to negotiate a permanent framework during the fall veto session.
key_facts.excerpt: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker on Friday plans to temporarily halt offering tax breaks to data centers that apply to build in the state and intends to call on lawmakers and other groups to hash out a framework in the fall veto session for how the centers should be developed.

key_facts.fact: Since 2019, Illinois has incentivized data-center development, and at least 27 data centers have received incentives totaling $983 million in estimated lifetime tax breaks and benefits.
key_facts.excerpt: Since 2019, Illinois has incentivized data center developers to come to the state by offering tax credits, but Gov. JB Pritzker proposed suspending those in February. According to the state's 2024 report, at least 27 data centers had received incentives totaling $983 million in estimated lifetime tax breaks and benefits.

key_facts.fact: Pritzker's proposed framework would ban nondisclosure agreements between data centers and local governments, require regular energy and water use reporting, mandate community benefits agreements and require centers to 'go dark' when the grid is strained.
key_facts.excerpt: Banning nondisclosure agreements between data centers and local governments, Require data centers to regularly report their energy and water use, Require data centers to post public notice when applying for permits, Require data centers to enter community benefits agreements... have data centers go dark when the grid is strained.

key_facts.fact: The pause comes after the Illinois POWER Act, which would have curbed data-center development, was not called to a vote in the spring legislative session.
key_facts.excerpt: One bill that lawmakers did not address before the end of the Spring Session early Monday morning concerned data centers. Advocates said the POWER Act would curb 'unchecked data center development.' The POWER Act was not called to the floor.

stories.headline: Zelensky publishes open letter to Putin proposing meeting to end the war

key_facts.fact: On June 4, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky published an open letter to Vladimir Putin proposing that the two leaders meet to agree on an end to the war.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky published an open letter to President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in which he proposed the two leaders meet to agree an end to the war.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky urged Putin to set a date and venue and warned against prolonging the war into 2027 or 2028, citing intelligence assessments that Moscow is planning for years of continued hostilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Zelensky called on Putin to set a date and venue for the meeting and urged him not to prolong the war into 2027 or 2028, citing intelligence assessments that suggest Moscow is planning for years of continued hostilities.

key_facts.fact: Putin, speaking to reporters at the St. Petersburg International Economic Forum, said he did not rule out signing a peace deal with Zelensky if an agreement could be reached and was 'willing to make some compromises.'
key_facts.excerpt: Speaking to reporters in St Petersburg, Putin said he did not rule out signing a peace deal with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky, if an agreement could be reached... Russian President Vladimir Putin has said that he is willing to make some compromises to end the war in Ukraine and strike a peace deal.

key_facts.fact: Overnight on June 4-5, Russia launched two Kh-59/69 guided missiles and 216 Shahed-type drones at Ukraine; air defenses intercepted 198 UAVs. At least 11 people were killed and 68 injured over the past day.
key_facts.excerpt: Russian forces launched two Kh-59/69 guided missiles and 216 Shahed-type attack drones against Ukraine overnight, with Ukrainian air defenses intercepting 198 of the unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs)... At least 11 people were killed and 68 injured in Russian attacks across Ukraine over the past day.

key_facts.fact: Zelensky's letter argued that ordinary Russians have grown tired of Ukrainian missile and drone attacks, inflation and fuel shortages and were ready for peace.
key_facts.excerpt: In his letter, Zelensky said the majority of Russians had grown tired of Ukrainian missile and drones attacks, inflation and fuel shortages, and were ready for peace.
